review.summary:
Round 3, TESTS AND EVIDENCE lens, on b007ff3 (HEAD aaad29d adds only a carry note). target/debug/planroom was built after the last code commit: its catalogue hash 7a8e3030… matches plugin/scripts/engine.env and packages/contract's CATALOGUE_HASH.

What I ran:
- The binary on copies of target/e2e/fixture/shop under the scratchpad, with PLANROOM_DATA set to a scratch directory.
- packages/mod/src/guard.ts and guard.test.ts under `node --experimental-strip-types`, with a CATALOGUE stub and a minimal vitest shim. Every list passed except 2 cases that fail only because of my stub.
- tests/installer/run.sh with TMPDIR set to the scratchpad and a loopback server only: 21 passed, 0 failed.

I did not run cargo, pnpm, vitest, Playwright or `claude plugin test`. Where I say a test "would" do something, I reasoned it from the code.

Fix check for each round-2 material finding in this lens:
- **tests-r2-1: holds in the plan, not in feature_list.json.**
  - architecture.md:1021, 1276 and 1641 and DR-86 move `map` paging into M1's S1 slice.
  - The binary still cuts the fixture at component level (20 of 38 blocks) and code level (21 of 83). It refuses `--cursor` as `invalid_argument`, which is expected until M1.
  - feature_list.json's S1 ci_path was never updated (tests-3-2).
- **tests-r2-2: holds.**
  - All 31 RECURSIVE_BYPASSES are denied, including every tests-r2-2 string, as are all 18 security-3 BYPASSES and all 32 WRITE_BYPASSES. Both everyday lists pass.
  - plugin-tests/guard.test.tsx exercises the same rule through tool.check (read, not run).
  - The rule is a closed list of programs, and several recursive readers it doesn't name still pass (tests-3-3).

Spot-check of round 1's material fixes, all HOLD:
- **correctness-1 and unasked-3:** an uncommitted compose service and an untracked directory never reached the map.
- **drift-1:** `map --bogus --json` prints one `invalid_argument` envelope, exit 2.
- **ux-6:** an empty folder gives `no_repos`; map and focus agree, and the next action is `focus`.
- **ux-3:** the intent level gives `no_intent` with a way back.
- **unasked-8 and round 2's correctness-17 and unasked-r2-2:** a scan of a 60,000-file repo replied in 936 bytes, with `partial_scan` count 10000 and 10 sample paths. `schema --command` stayed under 1,500 tokens for every leaf (drift-r2-1).
- **ops-2:** the installer suite passes, including the new `a_swapped_cached_engine_is_refused`.
- **Golden:** the `focus` golden equals the current engine's output.
- **Scan behaviour:** a workspace with a map whose repos all become unreadable keeps its map, with one `repo_skipped` per repo.

Other checks:
- No feature_list.json entry is marked passing; all 32 are failing.
- Every test name that DR-86's Consequences cite exists.
- The test names that don't resolve match round 1's tests-3 count, so that gap hasn't grown.
- tests-r2-3 (the `first["warnings"]` assertion at scan.rs:334 that can't fail) is unchanged. It is a logged known gap, so I don't re-report it.

New: 1 material, 4 minor.

findings.title: The guard fails open when the host's $.env.get("HOME") gives nothing, and only mocked runs back it: the harness mocks HOME and fs.stat, and the last live run predates both guard rewrites
where: packages/mod/src/register.tsx:421-433 (places read once from $.env.get("HOME") and others)
packages/mod/plugin-tests/host.ts:175 (mock.env(on, { HOME: "/home/u" })) and :206-217 (fs.stat stub: every path is a file, realPath given)
docs/contributing/research/ws8-install.md:87-94 (the one live run of the real mod)
findings.evidence:
Verified:
- guard.ts:57 falls back to `/` when HOME is undefined. An empty string isn't caught either, because nonEmpty() isn't applied to HOME.
- I ran guard.ts with `guardPlaces("/work", {})`. The places came out as claudeConfig `//.claude`, dataRoot `//.local/share/planroom` and userConfig `//.config/planroom/config.toml`.
- With those places, all of these were ALLOWED: Read `/home/u/.claude/plugins/store/planroom_planroom-0123456789ab.json` (the person key), Read `/home/u/.config/planroom/config.toml`, `cat /home/u/.claude/plugins/store/planroom_x.json`, `cat ~/.claude/plugins/store/planroom_x.json` and `grep -r key /home/u/.claude`. Only state-directory names such as `/work/.planroom/store.db` stayed denied.
- Every guard unit test and plugin test supplies HOME through a stub: guard.test.ts:13 and host.ts:175. No test covers HOME being unset or empty.
- AGENTS.md (packages/mod) says `claude plugin test` mocks the environment, so a start-up change isn't proven until it runs live.
- The only live run is commit 91c2c67, 2026-10-26 12:24. It records room_query results and no guard denial. The guard was rewritten after it, in 8813f22 (13:06, security-3) and 8847df9 (15:09, GUARD2).

Assumed, not verified: whether Claude Code 2.1.310's `$.env.get("HOME")` returns the process's HOME. A-14 shows only that `$.env.get("CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT")` came back unset live.
findings.why: The guard is the only control between an agent and the person key in the mod's $.store, and the user config that may hold the gateway key. KICKOFF's "agents never act as a person" rests on it (DR-64, DR-75, C1, S9). As written, it fails open on an input that only a mock has ever supplied. A Read-tool call, which always takes an absolute path, would then reach the key. Round 2 rated the narrower recursive-read gap material (tests-r2-2), and this is the same exposure.
findings.fix: Fail closed: when HOME is undefined or empty, deny by the protected file names themselves wherever they sit (`*/plugins/store/planroom_*`, `*/planroom/config.toml`, `*/planroom/{ledger.db,open,backups,engine}`). Add a guard.test.ts case with `guardPlaces(cwd, {})` and with `HOME: ""`. Record one live denial (Read of the real $.store file) in ws8-install.md before M1 builds on the guard.

findings.title: tests-r2-1's fix never reached feature_list.json: S1's tier-A ci_path still runs the capped map with no paging step
where: docs/contributing/architecture.md:1021, 1641 (S1 slice: `--cursor` and `meta.next`, which the comparator follows)
findings.why: feature_list.json is the scenario's CI contract. An M1 implementer who follows it compares a cut map with TRUTH.components (24) and gets a spurious failure, or weakens the comparison. That is the defect tests-r2-1 was about.
findings.fix: Change S1's component and code steps to page with `--cursor` until there's no `meta.next`, and say the comparison runs on the concatenated pages. Add a planned test such as `s01_first_look.rs::the_comparator_pages_to_every_component`.

findings.title: The recursive-read rule and its bypass list cover a closed set of programs: git grep --no-index, ugrep -r, bsdtar, pax and gzip -r still read the person key's parent
findings.evidence:
I ran guard.ts with places cwd=/work and HOME=/home/u.

ALLOWED:
- `git grep --no-index key ~/.claude`
- `git -C ~ grep --no-index key .claude`
- `ugrep -r key ~/.claude`
- `bsdtar cf /tmp/a ~/.claude`
- `pax -w ~/.claude > /tmp/a`
- `gzip -rc ~/.claude > /tmp/x`
- `7z a /tmp/x ~/.config`

DENIED: `grep -r`, `egrep -r`, `grep -d recurse`, `ack`, `ag --hidden`, `cp -R`, `rsync -r`, `zip -r`, `tar -C ~ -c .claude`.

DR-86 accepts "programs that walk or write files themselves" as residual risk. Git's grep and ugrep are grep-family recursive readers, the class tests-r2-2 was about, and no test lists them.
findings.why: Residual risk on the person key (DR-75). It's minor because DR-86 already calls the guard a guardrail and names this class for SECURITY.md (M5).
findings.fix: Add `git grep --no-index` (and `git -C DIR grep`), `ugrep -r`, `bsdtar`, `pax` and `gzip -r` to the recursive-read rule and to RECURSIVE_BYPASSES. Or name these programs in DR-86's residual list, so SECURITY.md (M5) carries them.

findings.title: The M1 stand-in overlay's evidence names no commit, contradicting DR-86 and what the engine stores
findings.evidence:
Every overlay evidence_sample item is `{"type":"line",…,"commit":null,"branch":null}`.

DR-86 says Line and Ref evidence from a head scan name the commit and no branch. A fact read from a scanned fixture store has `"evidence":[{"type":"line","path":"kit/src/orderId.ts","line":1,…,"commit":"d77b…"`. That's a read-only sqlite query on the scratch copy's facts table.

This is the same class as tests-6 (overlay data contradicting the truth), and DR-86 made it newly wrong.
findings.why: The stand-in specs draw evidence popovers from data the engine can no longer produce. A canvas that broke on a non-null commit would still pass. Minor: test-only data.
findings.fix: Set each sample's `commit` to the fixture head of the repo it names, or drop the field. Note DR-86 in the overlay's `why`.

findings.title: budgets.rs claims to check the whole graph over HTTP but calls the app function in-process, so the route is never exercised
where: docs/contributing/architecture.md:1021 ("budgets.rs checks … the whole graph over HTTP")
findings.evidence: The test calls `planroom::app::map::for_canvas(&req, tmp.path())` directly, with no serve and no request. routes.rs:310 does call `for_canvas` today (read). If the route were moved to the capped `map::run`, or HTTP replies were sent through the CLI's `envelope_within`, no test would fail. The canvas e2e reads only the top level, which fits within the budget anyway.
findings.why: DR-86 rests the canvas's whole-graph promise on this test ("Replies over HTTP aren't checked, so --detail graph stays whole"), and architecture.md describes it as an HTTP check.
findings.fix: Have the test start `serve` (or call the axum router in-process) and POST /api/v1/map with level code and detail graph, then assert 2,000 nodes and no truncated warning. Or reword architecture.md:1021 to say it checks the app function.

verdicts.reason: The code defect is real, but material isn't supported. Verified: guard.ts:57 is `const home = env.HOME ?? "/"`, and nonEmpty() isn't applied to HOME. I copied guard.ts and the generated catalogue into the scratchpad and ran guardCall under node --experimental-strip-types. With guardPlaces("/work", {}) the places are `//.claude`, `//.local/share/planroom` and `//.config/planroom/config.toml`. These were ALLOWED: Read of /home/u/.claude/plugins/store/planroom_planroom-0123456789ab.json, Read of /home/u/.config/planroom/config.toml, `cat /home/u/.claude/plugins/store/planroom_x.json`, `cat ~/.claude/...` and `grep -r key /home/u/.claude`. With HOME "", the same calls were allowed except the `~` form. With HOME "/home/u", all of them were denied. host.ts:175 mocks `{ HOME: "/home/u" }` and guard.test.ts:13 fixes HOME, so no test covers a missing HOME. The live run (91c2c67, 12:24) predates 8813f22 (13:06) and 8847df9 (15:09) and records no denial. The HOME fallback was identical at 91c2c67. Why it's minor: the exposure needs the host's $.env.get("HOME") to return nothing. Nothing shows that, and the reviewer marks it as assumed. A-14's unset CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is a variable the host never sets (ws8-install.md:72 shows children get the session's env); it is not evidence that env.get filters variables. DR-86 (decisions.md:2109, 2145) and decisions.md:214 call the guard a guardrail, not a security boundary. So this is a hardening gap with a missing test, not a demonstrated exposure.

Confirmed. In feature_list.json, S1's ci_path steps still read `planroom map --level component --lens all --detail graph --json` and the container step, with no --cursor loop. S1's tests list has no paging test. Fix commit 71bd6ff touched only architecture.md and progress.md. architecture.md:1021 and :1641 now say M1's S1 slice adds --cursor and that the comparator follows meta.next. So the plan holds the fix and feature_list.json drifts from it. Round 2 verified the truncation (20 of 38 at component level) on the same binary. I didn't rerun it, because this finding is about the doc contract. Minor is right: the design home records the paging, and the comparator isn't built yet.

Reproduced with guard.ts under node, places cwd=/work and HOME=/home/u. ALLOWED: `git grep --no-index key ~/.claude`, `git -C ~ grep --no-index key .claude`, `ugrep -r key ~/.claude`, `bsdtar cf /tmp/a ~/.claude`, `pax -w ~/.claude > /tmp/a`, `gzip -rc ~/.claude > /tmp/x` and `7z a /tmp/x ~/.config`. DENIED: grep -r, egrep -r, grep -d recurse, ack, ag --hidden, cp -R, rsync -r, zip -r and tar -C ~ -c .claude. RECURSIVE_BYPASSES (guard.test.ts:327ff) lists none of the allowed forms. Minor is right: DR-86 (decisions.md:2145) accepts "programs that walk or write files themselves" as residual risk under a guardrail, bound for SECURITY.md.

Confirmed. tests/e2e/overlays/m1-tones-and-edges.map.json has 8 evidence_sample entries, every one with `"commit": null`. I scanned a scratch copy of target/e2e/fixture/shop with PLANROOM_DATA in a temp dir and PLANROOM_MODELS=off. Then I read store.db read-only: 109 line-evidence items, 0 with a null commit (e.g. commit d77bb654… and branch None), which matches DR-86's "Evidence names the commit" (decisions.md:2138). The overlay's `why` doesn't mention DR-86. This is test-only stand-in data, so minor.

Confirmed. budgets.rs:97-101 (the_canvas_graph_over_serve_takes_every_block) calls `planroom::app::map::for_canvas` in-process and starts no server. routes.rs:310 does route "map" to for_canvas today. The only test that POSTs /api/v1/map is server_auth.rs:124, at container level. The e2e specs request container or top level (surface.spec.ts:296-298, artifact.spec.ts:103), and the container level's 9 blocks fit the budget. So no test would fail if the route moved to the capped path. architecture.md:1021 says budgets.rs checks "the whole graph over HTTP", which drifts from the code. It's minor because the route is correct today and this is a test-coverage and doc gap.
